propositions: Rebar cannot reconcile against self-hosted Jira Data Center because the adapter is forked from Cloud, reaching into private implementation details and maintaining duplicate field maps and sanitizer logic.

Multiple independent copies of status/priority maps exist across adapters/jira/jira_fields.py, adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py, and rebar_reconciler/config.py, creating maintenance burden and allowing drift.

Cloud and Data Center differ on three critical axes—REST v2 vs v3, wiki/plain text vs ADF, PAT bearer auth vs ACLI, name-based vs accountId user identity—requiring parameterization by contract rather than code duplication.

Location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py) are loaded by path via dynamic loader and cannot relocate without breaking the loader, requiring shared logic to be achieved via dependency inversion and parameterization instead.

The Data Center backend must enforce TLS by default, reject cleartext URLs unless explicitly overridden with allow_insecure, never disable certificate verification, and require the PAT from environment only, never from config files.

A machine-checked import contract must structurally prevent the cross-adapter private imports and logic duplication that caused the original fork, blocking CI if adapters/jira_datacenter imports adapters/jira or if adapters/jira_family imports either adapter.
